Appreciate you opening this — and glad hermes-talk lands close to what you sketched in NousResearch/hermes-agent#53836. That issue was the direct inspiration for the plugin, so having you file the first feature request here feels right.

Gemini Live is the natural second backend, and you picked the right moment to ask. Some honest scoping:

**What's already provider-agnostic:** the run-control surface (list_agents / steer_agent / stop_work), the receipt ledger (queued vs landed vs missed), and the Hermes tool dispatch. None of that cares which realtime transport is underneath.

**What's OpenAI-shaped today:** the realtime loop itself — session setup, audio framing, barge-in handling all speak OpenAI Realtime. Adding Gemini Live means cutting a provider seam through that loop, not just swapping an endpoint.

That seam is exactly what NousResearch/hermes-agent#77111 (RealtimeVoiceProvider RFC) proposes at the Hermes level — your request here is the concrete second-provider case that RFC needed. I'd rather build the Gemini backend against that abstraction than hand-roll a second transport in the plugin, so I've linked the two.

Near-term the roadmap has the steer nonce token (#1) and async stop (#2) ahead of this, but it's on the list. One scoping question so I sequence it right: which matters most to you first — the speech-to-speech loop on a free AI Studio key, or the live vision/screen-share piece? Those are separable, and audio-first would ship much sooner.

Yeah, saw the release — great day for Hermes voice all around. Worth being precise about what 0.20's "Talk to Hermes" is, because it's a different shape than this plugin:

**0.20 voice mode** is the turn-based pipeline made conversational: STT → model → clause-by-clause streaming TTS, with barge-in and wake words. Big upgrade, and honestly worth using today.

**hermes-talk** is one realtime duplex audio session: the model hears audio directly (no transcription step in the conversation loop), tool calls happen inside the speech layer, and background agents report back out loud mid-conversation. The README calls this out — turn-based is the right shape for plenty of work; this is the other shape. 0.20 doesn't change that split, and it doesn't add Gemini Live either (the new Gemini entries are text models in the catalogs).

On cost, two honest paths for you:

1. **Today, free-ish:** if you're on any paid ChatGPT plan and signed into the Codex CLI, hermes-talk needs no API key and has no per-minute bill — it mints the realtime session off your subscription's own entitlement. The $20 plan should work (the OAuth mint is the same flow on every paid tier); OpenAI doesn't publish the entitlement quotas so I won't promise limits, but if you try it and hit a wall, that's exactly the data point I want.

2. **The real answer for your use case:** the Gemini Live backend, since AI Studio's free tier is the whole appeal. Your "not forcing a sequence" is noted and appreciated — with free usage as the driver, audio-first Gemini Live is the practical target once #1 and #2 clear.

Thanks for the release heads-up and the kind words. Keep the requests coming.

Shipped in v0.6.0: every steered note now travels as `[tk-xxxxxxxx] note` (both verbs — steer_agent and the new redirect_agent share the composer), and the drain-preview match is token-first. Two live agents holding identical text can no longer land each other's receipts — the false-positive path this issue existed to kill is structurally dead. Kimi's v0.6 gate confirmed the closure. Bonus hardening the same release: receipts whose token still sits in the agent's pending queue at drain-log time are excluded from the batch sweep (the drained-then-requeued race, Codex r1-4/r2-1).

v0.6.0 partial: the third item (proactive landed speech) is now half-covered — subagent completions are announced into the live call push-style via the subagent_stop hook (injection-contained: system item + tool_choice:none + self-deleting). Specifically-"your note landed" speech is still pull-at-check_work. Items 1-2 (api_server stop POST off the mic thread, terminate() polling to completion) remain untouched and keep this open.

Shipped in v0.6.1: (1) both stop verbs run on daemon workers with a 1.5s bounded courtesy wait — the fast path speaks the real result, a slow server gets honest detached wording, and the receipt is PERSISTED (tee'd to the JSONL history) so it survives hang-up and restart; (2) terminate() is confirmed against a handle captured before the signal (immune to the worker reaping first), with a terminal-record fallback before any uncertainty claim; (3) landed notes are pushed — the ledger's set_landed_notifier seam marshals onto the session loop and speaks 'the note just landed' through the serialized announcement pump. One Codex adversarial round on the release found the durability, reaped-handle, and interleaving gaps; all three closed in-release with regression tests. 390 tests.

Shipped in v0.6.1: the borrow has a full lifecycle. Every ensure reconciles — operator turns verbose logging on at runtime and the gate is removed with the found level restored (their config governs); toggles it back off and the borrow is re-taken, so the watcher never sits blind behind a stale True. uninstall_watchers() is the production unhook: symmetric detach of both handlers, the gate filter, and the borrowed level, receipts kept (history, not wiring) — ready to wire to a host plugin-unload hook when Hermes grows one.

Code landmarks (flat top-level modules, see pyproject py-modules):
- `talk_operator_auth.py` — the existing speaker-authority layer. Closed issue #10 (every speaker treated as operator) is the prior art; this issue moves enforcement so the HOST validates a minted principal proof at canonical execution, instead of trusting upstream labels.

**Implementation context (orchestrator recon, 2026-08-17):**

Code landmarks: `talk_core_realtime.py` / `talk_openai_realtime.py` (Realtime session + response lifecycle), `talk_core_session.py` (session state), `talk_audio.py` (playback drain), `talk_relay.py` (Discord audio relay), `talk_steer.py` (interruption/steering — closed issues #1, #2, #5, #6, #7 are the steering prior art and show the house style for lifecycle state machines + nonce correlation).

The fix wants a single-owner response state machine per Talk generation: distinguish response-accepted / transcript-final / playback-drained / cancelled / conversation-complete as separate states; barge-in cancels exactly the active response and fences late events by generation+response id (same nonce-correlation pattern as closed #1).

Test doctrine: offline deterministic — scripted Realtime transcripts (existing test style), no audio device, no network. Cover: late starts, duplicate terminal events, announcement races, reconnect, close.

Upstream already provides the data — this is a consumption feature, not an upstream request. Verified against the Hermes docs (hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/api-server):
- `GET /v1/skills` — installed skills with metadata (same substrate as the skills hub)
- `GET /v1/toolsets` — toolsets resolved for the platform, with `enabled`, `configured`, and the concrete `tools` list each expands to
- `GET /v1/capabilities` — machine-readable feature flags (`run_events_sse`, `run_approval`, session endpoints…) meant exactly for external orchestrators
- `GET /health/detailed` — bounded readiness incl. active runs/delegations counts
All bearer-authed via `API_SERVER_KEY`; in-process, the plugin `ctx` surface is the alternative (hermes-talk is a `register(ctx)` plugin — prefer in-process reads off the committed host attachment where possible, REST as fallback).

The issue's own requirements stay the contract: distinguish installed vs callable vs configured vs authenticated; refresh on reconnect + invalidate stale snapshots; bounded + redacted + profile-authorized; catalog access grants no authority.

Test doctrine: offline — fake catalog payloads, no live gateway in CI.

**Recon (orchestrator, 2026-08-17): the event stream exists upstream — per-lane reality.** Verified against the hermes-agent source and hermes-talk main.

**api_server lane — no upstream change needed.** `talk_apiserver.py:355-375` polls `GET /v1/runs/{id}` every 1s, while the SAME server already exposes `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events` (SSE; hermes-agent `gateway/platforms/api_server.py:1975, 6678`) with exactly this issue's vocabulary: `tool.started` / `tool.completed` (tool, duration, error) / `reasoning.available` / `subagent.start` / `subagent.complete` (goal, child_session_id, cost, output_tail) / `message.delta` / `approval.request` / `approval.responded` / `run.completed|failed|cancelled`. Same `API_SERVER_KEY` bearer auth the plugin already holds (`talk_apiserver.py:64, 314-319`).

**SSE caveats to design around:** single-consumer `asyncio.Queue` — a disconnect destroys the buffer and a second subscriber steals events; ~1s subscribe window after `POST /v1/runs` before 404; unsubscribed buffers swept at 300s; terminal status retained 1h. Keep the existing 1s poll as fallback — `GET /v1/runs/{id}` already carries a `last_event` field the plugin currently ignores.

**Detached `hermes -z` lane — NO event surface** (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py:424-449` wires no callbacks). Durable fallbacks that exist today: the `async_delegations` table in HERMES_HOME/state.db (state, timestamps, result_json, delivery_state — best durable poll target); the `sessions`/`messages` tables (a `-z` child DOES write them, but prints no session id — correlation by started_at/cwd needed); `cache/delegation/live/<id>/task-N.log` append-only live logs (human text, delegate_task only).

**Plugin hook bus:** `subagent_start`/`subagent_stop` only (`hermes_cli/plugins.py:164-165`; fire sites `tools/delegate_tool.py:1596, 2699`) — hermes-talk already subscribes in `talk_lifecycle.py`. No progress events, no cross-process delivery.

**Evidence the upstream contract is missing for the rest:** `talk_steer.py:275-300` attaches a logging.Handler to the host's run_agent logger and regex-scrapes lines — a log-scraping oracle that only exists because no structured feed does.

**Suggested build order:** consume the SSE stream on the api_server lane first (pure local change, satisfies most acceptance criteria), poll fallback retained; `-z` lane rides state.db `async_delegations` polling until the smallest upstream contract lands (file that at NousResearch per this issue's closing note).

**Recon (orchestrator, 2026-08-17):** announcement triggers ride the same event sources mapped in the #33 recon comment — read that first. The announcement-worthy events already exist on the api_server SSE stream: `run.completed|failed|cancelled`, `subagent.complete`, and `approval.request` (hermes-agent `gateway/platforms/api_server.py:6162-6250`). For exact-once recovery after reconnect, the durable `async_delegations` table already carries a `delivery_state` column (`tools/async_delegation.py:119-179`) — persist announcement delivery against it rather than inventing a parallel store.

**Recon (orchestrator, 2026-08-17):** the durable substrate for exact return routes already exists upstream: HERMES_HOME/state.db `async_delegations` (`delegation_id, state, dispatched_at, completed_at, result_json, task_json, owner_pid, delivery_state` — `tools/async_delegation.py:119-179`, read API `get_durable_delegation()` / `list_async_delegations()`). The detach hole this issue fixes is real and measurable: talk-runs.jsonl on this box has three runs stuck at `running` forever, and a detached `hermes -z` child writes state.db `sessions`/`messages` but prints no session id (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py:3`), so today nothing can correlate the child back to the Talk session that spawned it — that correlation IS the return route this issue mints.

## 🔍 Investigation: enforce operator speaker authority at canonical host execution

**Type**: `ENHANCEMENT`

### Assessment

| Metric | Value | Reasoning |
|--------|-------|-----------|
| Priority | `HIGH` | Blocks epic #32's security invariant ("immutable operator is the only mutating speaker by default"); the host execution path currently has zero authorization checks. |
| Complexity | `MEDIUM` | 2 production files changed (`talk_cli.py`, `talk_operator_auth.py`), 1 new test file; touches a well-defined seam with an existing pattern to mirror. |
| Confidence | `HIGH` | The gap is unambiguous: `HostExecutionRelay.handle_tool_batch_async()` never reads the trusted binding keys that `bind_tool_event()` attaches; the fix mirrors the relay-path pattern validated by 35+ existing tests. |

---

### Problem Statement

The authorization ledger (`DiscordToolAuthorizationLedger`) fully enforces operator-only mutation for the legacy relay path. But the canonical host execution path (via `HostExecutionRelay`) bypasses the ledger entirely. `bind_tool_event()` stamps every `FunctionCall` with trusted binding data (line 1018-1019), but `HostExecutionRelay.handle_tool_batch_async()` extracts only `response_id`, `item_id`, `call_id`, `name`, and `arguments` — ignoring `_talk_speaker_binding`, `_talk_response_authority`, and `_talk_call_permit`.

---

### Root Cause Analysis

WHY: Non-operator can execute mutating tools through host execution path
↓ BECAUSE: `HostExecutionRelay.handle_tool_batch_async()` never calls `authorize_tool()`
  → Evidence: `talk_cli.py:494-530`

↓ BECAUSE: `HostExecutionRelay` accepts no `tool_authorizer` callback
  → Evidence: `talk_cli.py:478-482` — constructor takes only `attachment`

↓ ROOT CAUSE: Host bridge (`b2c48dd`) was added after the ledger (`8e3e2ec`) but never wired to it
  → Evidence: `talk_cli.py:955-964` — routing decision passes no authorizer

CONTRAST: `RealtimeRelay._tool_result()` at `talk_relay.py:440-446` calls `self.tool_authorizer(name, event)` before executing — this is the exact pattern to mirror.

---

### Implementation Plan

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1 | `talk_cli.py:478-482` | Add `tool_authorizer` kwarg to `HostExecutionRelay.__init__()` |
| 2 | `talk_cli.py:500-522` | Check `tool_authorizer(name, event)` before `mint_tool_call_permit()`; denied → output denial, `continue` |
| 3 | `talk_cli.py:955-964` | Pass `authorization_ledger.authorize_tool` to `HostExecutionRelay` constructor |
| 4 | `tests/test_host_authority.py` | New test file: operator pass, non-operator deny, read-only pass, unclassified fail-closed, mixed speakers, missing attribution, spoofed provider identity, replayed proofs, session-generation drift |

<details>
<summary>📋 Detailed Implementation Steps</summary>

**Step 1 — `HostExecutionRelay.__init__`** (mirror `RealtimeRelay` pattern):
```python
def __init__(self, attachment, *, tool_authorizer=None) -> None:
    self.attachment = attachment
    self.tool_authorizer = tool_authorizer
```

**Step 2 — Authorization check in `handle_tool_batch_async`** (after argument validation, before permit minting):
```python
if self.tool_authorizer is not None:
    denial = self.tool_authorizer(event.get("name", ""), event)
    if denial is not None:
        outputs[position] = self._output(event["call_id"], denial)
        continue
```
`authorize_tool()` consumes the call permit internally (line 471-472), preventing replay. Denied events never reach the host attachment.

**Step 3 — Wiring at routing decision** (same callable the relay path uses):
```python
HostExecutionRelay(
    host_execution_attachment,
    tool_authorizer=(
        authorization_ledger.authorize_tool
        if authorization_ledger is not None
        else None
    ),
)
```

**Step 4 — Tests** cover every acceptance criterion: operator can mutate, non-operator denied, read-only available to all, unclassified fails closed, mixed speakers denied, missing attribution denied, provider metadata cannot satisfy authority, replayed proofs consumed, session-generation drift invalidates old proofs. All fully offline using `FakeProviderSession` + `HostExecutionAttachment`.

</details>

---

### Scope Boundaries

**In scope**: Wire `authorize_tool` into `HostExecutionRelay`; comprehensive offline tests.

**Out of scope**: Action-approval semantics (#37), response serialization (#38), `talk_host.py` HostAdapter, `talk_operator_auth.py` logic, `talk_wire.py`, `talk_discord.py`.

*Investigated by Claude • 2026-08-17T21:31Z*

**Feasibility + prior-art recon (orchestrator, 2026-08-17). Verdict: plugin-only — no upstream PR needed.**

**Hermes upstream:** core voice is uniformly turn-based (VAD STT → LLM turn → streamed TTS; the desktop app already has mic capture + barge-in for THAT mode). True duplex realtime exists nowhere in core: the RealtimeVoiceProvider ABC PR (NousResearch/hermes-agent#81404) self-closed with zero maintainer engagement, its RFC (#77111) got no maintainer response, and core's de facto answer to duplex voice (#53836) is 'install hermes-talk.' Precedent for a plugin-owned transport: our own Discord bridge (fully plugin-owned socket). The one gap: core's `/api/audio/speak-stream` WS is TTS-out-only and transcription is batch-only — mic-frames-IN is a new plugin-side endpoint, not a core blocker.

**Prior art (OpenClaw, MIT, 386k★):** their transport contract is proven across 5+ channels and is the shape to adopt: `TalkTransport = webrtc | provider-websocket | gateway-relay | managed-room` with ONE canonical event envelope (`session.*/turn.*/capture.*/transcript.*/output.audio.*/tool.*`) — `openclaw/openclaw` `src/talk/talk-events.ts`. Notably they do NOT unify speaker identity across transports — each channel plugin owns its own speaker model (`extensions/discord/src/voice/speaker-context.ts`). That division of labor matches our #39 authority design: copy it, don't force one cross-transport speaker schema.

**Prior-art recon (orchestrator, 2026-08-17): the roster-orchestrator is genuinely unbuilt territory — and the seed pattern exists.**

OpenClaw (MIT, 386k★) confirmed by code inspection: a voice session resolves to exactly ONE agent (`src/talk/agent-target.ts` `resolveTalkTargetAgentId`), and voice control only steers/cancels that same agent. No surface lets voice address multiple named agents and get results announced back — i.e., this epic's core idea has no incumbent even in the biggest OSS agent framework.

Patterns to port rather than invent:
- `openclaw_agent_consult` single-tool delegation contract (`src/talk/agent-consult-tool.ts`): one stable tool name, closed exposure policy (`safe-read-only`/`owner`/`none`), `confirmationId` round-trip for spoken high-impact confirmations. Extend with `params.agentId` selecting from the Bot roster.
- `src/talk/forced-consult-coordinator.ts`: dedupe for the native-tool-call-vs-relay-fallback race — a roster orchestrator hits this race N times harder.
- `src/talk/agent-talkback-runtime.ts`: debounced talkback queue with hard caps (32 pending / 32KB) — the memory-bounding shape for N agents' pending announcements (#34's queue, per-target).

**Prior-art recon (orchestrator, 2026-08-17):** two lessons from OpenClaw (MIT, 386k★), which ships 17 TTS + 5 STT + 3 native-S2S providers behind one surface.

1. **Copy the capability-negotiation object, not just a provider registry:** `RealtimeVoiceProviderCapabilities` (`src/talk/provider-types.ts:164-177`) — `supportsBargeIn` vs `handlesInputAudioBargeIn` (client-guessed vs provider-confirmed interruption — a real distinction), `supportsActivationNameGating`, `supportsToolCalls`, `supportsSessionResumption`, `supportsVideoFrames`. Plus their 3-way capability split (`speechProviders` / `realtimeTranscriptionProviders` / `realtimeVoiceProviders`) so a provider can be TTS-only (ElevenLabs), realtime-STT-only, or native-S2S without special-case branches.

2. **Draw the in-tree vs external-plugin line BEFORE the provider list grows.** OpenClaw closed four provider PRs (local Whisper #115698, AWS bundle #90792, SenseAudio TTS #81834, Teams #91438/#91107) with 'belongs in the plugin marketplace, not core' — and enforces it with a review bot. For hermes-talk: in-tree = OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live (#22), ONE reference cascaded provider; everything else = out-of-tree via the provider contract.

**Web recon addendum (2026-08-17):** the closest existing reference implementation for this epic is Pipecat's subagents framework (`pipecat-ai/pipecat-subagents`, since merged into core Pipecat) — distributed multi-agent with handoff, parallel dispatch, and timeout-cancel semantics on a realtime voice loop. Read it before designing the roster-dispatch layer; it is the only found system that keeps the voice loop live while N children work.

**Web recon (2026-08-17):** the 'speak only at an interruption-safe opening' requirement has an existing reference design: `protoLabsAI/protoVoice` ships a delivery-policy inbox — each announcement carries a priority class (NOW / NEXT_SILENCE / WHEN_ASKED) and delivery is bid-then-drain at silence boundaries. That is almost exactly this issue's spec; steal the policy taxonomy and the bid-then-drain drain loop, and pair it with OpenClaw's bounded talkback-queue caps (see the #43 recon comment).

**Web recon addendum (2026-08-17):** for the transport CONTRACT itself, the cleanest shape found is the OpenAI Agents SDK `RealtimeTransportLayer` interface — five verbs, five real implementations (WebRTC, WebSocket, SIP, Cloudflare Workers, Twilio), and an official 'bring your own transport' extension path. Combine: Agents SDK's minimal verb surface + OpenClaw's event envelope taxonomy + per-transport speaker identity (previous comment) = the #44 design brief in three citations.

**Web recon addendum (2026-08-17):** Pipecat is the existence proof that cascaded (STT→LLM→TTS) and native speech-to-speech can live behind ONE abstraction — both are literally the same processor-list `Pipeline` type, with `RealtimeServiceMetadataFrame` carrying the provider-mode differences. Among Pipecat/LiveKit/Vocode/TEN it is the only framework where the two modes share a single pipeline shape — imitate its transport-vs-pipeline-vs-provider separation when implementing the cascaded provider behind the #20 session contract.

## MEDIUM Issues (Needs Decision)

### 1. `discard_tool_event` permit consumption not tested through HostExecutionRelay

**Agent**: test-coverage | `talk_cli.py:493`

`discard_tool_event` consumes permits when queued events are discarded, but no test exercises this through `HostExecutionRelay`. The equivalent `RealtimeRelay` path IS tested in `test_operator_auth.py:490`. If the delegation were accidentally removed, discarded events would retain permits — replay vulnerability.

**Options**: Fix now (LOW effort, ~12-line test) | Create issue | Skip (RealtimeRelay equivalent tested)

<details>
<summary>Suggested test</summary>

```python
def test_discard_consumes_permit_through_host_path(monkeypatch):
    ledger = talk_operator_auth.DiscordToolAuthorizationLedger()
    ledger.record_packet(_speaker(OPERATOR_ID), _pcm(20))
    _bind_response(ledger)
    event = _make_tool_event(ledger, call_id="call-discard")
    monkeypatch.setenv("TALK_DISCORD_OPERATOR_USER_IDS", str(OPERATOR_ID))

    attachment = HostExecutionAttachment()
    relay = talk_cli.HostExecutionRelay(
        attachment, tool_authorizer=ledger.authorize_tool
    )
    relay.discard_tool_event(event)
    results = _run_batch(relay, [event])

    assert len(attachment.minted) == 0
    assert any("not run" in cmd.output for cmd in results[0])
```

</details>

## Investigation: serialize Realtime responses and eliminate duplicate or cut-off speech

**Type**: `BUG`

### Assessment

| Metric | Value | Reasoning |
|--------|-------|-----------|
| Severity | `HIGH` | The live voice path (`RealtimeRelay.handle_realtime_event`) has no response-identity fencing at all — it forwards every audio/transcript event unconditionally regardless of which response produced it. Major, user-facing break in core turn-taking with no workaround short of restarting the session; stops short of CRITICAL since nothing crashes or loses data. |
| Complexity | `HIGH` | Root cause spans the neutral event contract (`talk_realtime.py`), its OpenAI decoder (`talk_openai_realtime.py`), the shared CLI/Discord event loop (`talk_relay.py`), and orchestration in `talk_cli.py` — plus a real architectural wrinkle: `RealtimeRelay` has two parallel dispatch paths and only one is actually live. |
| Confidence | `HIGH` | Every link in the causal chain is verified directly against source, not summarized. The one external-API assumption the fix depends on (OpenAI's audio/transcript delta events carry `response_id`) is confirmed against OpenAI's own API reference, not inferred from naming. |

---

### Two landmark corrections (matters for anyone implementing this)

- **`talk_relay.py` is not Discord-specific** — it's the transport-agnostic `RealtimeRelay` event loop shared by the terminal CLI and Discord. The actual Discord audio sink (`DiscordAudio` in `talk_discord.py`) is a pure downstream consumer with no role in response-completion signaling.
- **`talk_steer.py` has no code path in common with voice interruption** — it's delivery-receipt tracking for `/steer` text notes to background coding subagents. It's still the right *pattern* reference (nonce/correlation, named states, fail-open on ambiguity), just not code to extend.
- Bonus finding: `RealtimeRelay` has two parallel dispatch mechanisms (`handle_event`/`_DISPATCH` vs `handle_realtime_event`). **Only `handle_realtime_event` is used by the live session** — the existing `test_barge_in_cancels_and_drains` test (today's best evidence of this bug) currently exercises the path production doesn't run. The plan below fixes both, sharing logic via one helper so they can't drift again.

### Root cause

OpenAI's Realtime API assigns every response a `response_id` and echoes it on every event belonging to that response — including `response.output_audio.delta` and `response.output_audio_transcript.delta`, both of which are **guaranteed to keep arriving after a response is cancelled** (confirmed against OpenAI's own API reference, not assumed). `talk_openai_realtime.decode_event` discards `response_id` when mapping these to neutral events (`talk_openai_realtime.py:207-233`), and the neutral `OutputAudio`/`Transcript` dataclasses have no field to carry it even if it were kept (`talk_realtime.py:136-157`). Downstream, `RealtimeRelay` tracks only a single boolean (`response_active`) and one clobberable scalar (`last_audio_item_id`) — never *which* response is active (`talk_relay.py:188-297`). The result: a cancelled response's still-arriving tail audio and transcript deltas get played and transcribed indiscriminately alongside the next response's — the exact duplicate/overlapping/cut-off speech reported.

A secondary, related gap: `pump_announcements`'s busy-gate (`talk_cli.py:584-612`) is check-then-act with no re-check inside the actual send's critical section — its own docstring already names this exact race ("Codex v0.6.1 finding 3") as a known, only-partially-closed gap.

### Compaction failure inside `_append_history_strict` is indistinguishable from a write failure — silently strands delivered results, and the fail-closed branch has zero test coverage
📍 `talk_runs.py:183-204` (`_append_history_strict`), `talk_runs.py:522-544` (`_claim_delivery_in_history`)

`_claim_delivery_in_history` writes the `"delivery": "delivered"` record durably *before* compaction runs. If compaction then throws (e.g. a Windows `os.replace` losing a file-lock race against the dashboard lane writing the same history file concurrently), the function returns `False` and the result never gets announced — but because the delivered record is already on disk, `list_undelivered_for_session` filters it out on every future reconnect. **The result is permanently, silently lost, marked "delivered" when it was never spoken.** This is the direct counterpart to `start_run`'s acceptance-write failure, which *is* tested — the delivery-side equivalent has zero coverage, which is exactly why the bug wasn't caught by the PR's own mutation-testing pass.

```python
def _append_history_strict(record: dict) -> None:
    """Fail-CLOSED tee, for the acceptance record only (hermes-talk#35)."""
    if not _history_enabled():
        return
    with _HISTORY_LOCK:
        path = _history_path()
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        # Compaction is maintenance, not this record's durability contract —
        # the write above already landed.
        try:
            if path.stat().st_size > _HISTORY_MAX_BYTES:
                _compact_history_locked(path)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — compaction is best-effort
            _log.warning("talk run history compaction failed: %s", exc)
```

## Correction: the end-of-turn frame is now just the documented close

The original version of this PR sent `{"text": "", "flush": true}` as the end-of-turn frame. **That shape appears nowhere in ElevenLabs' documentation**, and it has been removed (`71f0a53`, prose caught up in `04e2b68`). Recording the research here rather than leaving it in a transcript, because the next person to read this code will be tempted to re-add it.

### The load-bearing fact: this lane's socket is PER TURN

`talk_cascade_voice.py` opens and closes one socket per response — `_stream()` calls `self._connect()` at the top and `ws.close()` in its `finally`, and `_run()`'s docstring says "one stream run speaks one response". The dashboard relay builds a fresh `CascadeVoice` per POST ("one POST == one response's speech"). Nothing is held across turns.

That matters because **closing is documented to flush**:

> "In addition, closing the websocket will automatically force generate any buffered text."
> — [realtime TTS guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/websockets/realtime-tts), "Buffering"

So the empty-text EOS frame this lane *already* sent on every turn is the end-of-turn trigger. Nothing needed to replace `try_trigger_generation`; the flush was solving a problem the close already solved.

`test_each_response_opens_and_closes_its_own_socket` now pins that fact — two responses, two distinct sockets, both closed. It is what fails first if anyone makes the socket persistent, because at that point the last partial chunk of every answer would sit buffered until the *next* answer pushed it out.

### Why not an explicit flush frame

Three findings, each from ElevenLabs' own docs:

1. **Their flush example carries real text**, not empty text — [realtime TTS guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/websockets/realtime-tts), "Buffering":
   ```python
   websocket.send(json.dumps({"text": "Generate this audio immediately.", "flush": True}))
   ```
2. **`text` is REQUIRED on `SendText`** — from the OpenAPI schema embedded in the [stream-input reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/v-1-text-to-speech-voice-id-stream-input):
   ```yaml
   SendText:
     properties: {text: {...}, ...}
     required:
       - text
   ```
   And an empty-text frame is a *different* message, `CloseConnection`. Their Tips section states the convention outright: a single space `" "` is valid content/keep-alive, while `""` closes the socket.
3. **A combined `{"text": "", "flush": true}` occurs zero times** in either the realtime guide or the stream-input reference (grepped both raw HTML for empty-text co-occurring with flush: no matches).

So on single-context `/stream-input` there is **no schema-legal way to force generation without either real text or the close.** The frame we were sending mixed two mutually-exclusive documented shapes — it worked live, but "works today" on an undocumented shape is exactly what breaks on a server deploy.

An earlier suggestion of `{"text": " ", "flush": true}` (whitespace instead of empty) was checked too and also has zero occurrences in their docs, so it was not adopted either.

### The alternative, for the record

Their sibling `/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/multi-stream-input` endpoint *does* define exactly the frame a persistent-socket design would need — `FlushContextClient`, where `text` is **optional**:

```yaml
FlushContextClient:
  properties:
    context_id: {type: string}
    text: {type: string, optional: true}
    flush: {type: boolean}
  required: [context_id, flush]
```

with closing handled by its own explicit `CloseContextClient` message, never implied by empty text. LiveKit's production ElevenLabs plugin targets that endpoint and uses exactly this pattern. **No issue filed for a migration**, because this lane's per-turn socket means there is nothing left unsolved — the note above and the socket test are the durable record if that ever changes.

### What this changed

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| text chunk | `{"text": "...", "try_trigger_generation": true}` | `{"text": "..."}` |
| end of turn | `{"text": "", "flush": true}` | `{"text": ""}` — the documented `CloseConnection`, which flushes |

The actual fix in this PR is unchanged and is the one that matters: **no per-chunk generation trigger**, so the model buffers on its own `chunk_length_schedule` and carries intonation across sentence boundaries. Plus `enable_ssml_parsing` and the `voice_settings` / `TALK_CASCADE_SPEED` surface.

Tests updated accordingly: no frame carries a `flush` key at all, the EOS is exactly `{"text": ""}` and is the last frame, and every frame between BOS and EOS is a bare text frame.

Thanks for shipping #249. You asked which hold value works here. On this HDMI TV it's **700 ms**, with `TALK_ECHO_GATE_RATIO=0.1`, and it has been since 12/11. I didn't A/B 200 ms in a real session. Measured TV latency is ~200 ms, but the echo tail lasts longer than that.

But the hold turned out not to be the whole story on a TV. Three findings from re-measuring with v0.25.0 (same TV and webcam mic), in case they're useful for the docs or the gate defaults:

**1. The barge-in floor goes stale.** `TALK_ECHO_GATE_MIN_BARGE_IN_LEVEL` is an absolute level, so it is only valid for the speaker volume it was measured at.
- On 12/11 the echo peaked at 0.003 and a floor of 0.02 had plenty of margin.
- By 21/11 the echo of the agent's *speech* peaked at 0.016–0.024 (100 ms block RMS), so the 0.02 floor let echo through.
- The agent answered itself again. The user-side transcripts came out as fragments of its own sentences, some of them in Spanish.

Calibrating with noise hides this. At the same volume, speech gave an echo of 0.016–0.024, while speech-band noise gave 0.009 and low-frequency noise 0.005. The webcam (Logitech Brio 500) suppresses stationary noise but passes speech. Calibrate with speech.

**2. On TV + webcam, the operator's voice and the echo arrive at about the same level.**
- I set the floor to 0.08. That ended the self-replies. On the **Gemini** lane, voice barge-in then stopped working while the agent talked (live session today), and the Live model still told the operator they could interrupt it at any time.
- Later the same day, with the **same gate settings** on the **OpenAI** lane (`gpt-realtime-2.1`), the operator *could* interrupt mid-sentence and the model followed. I haven't isolated why. A likely candidate is that the Live protocol has no client cancel/truncate (as `talk_gemini_realtime.py` documents), while OpenAI does. It's worth knowing for TV setups.

**3. AEC doesn't rescue this setup, and installing `pactl` would make it worse.** I measured PipeWire's `libpipewire-module-echo-cancel` with `aec/libspa-aec-webrtc`. I loaded it in a standalone `pipewire -c` process, played the test speech through its sink, and recorded the raw and cancelled mic together. `pw-link -l` confirmed the routing.

| | raw mic | after AEC |
|---|---|---|
| noise floor | 0.0010 | 0.0001 |
| echo peak, run 1 | 0.0167 | 0.0162 |
| echo peak, run 2 | 0.0139 | 0.0150 |

The coherence between the played speech and the mic is only 0.12–0.23 (1 s windows, 100 Hz–8 kHz), and the delay jitters ±10 ms from window to window. A least-squares FIR fitted offline on the same recording gets -0.7 dB. Whatever the TV and the webcam do to the sound is nonlinear, so a linear canceller can't remove it.

That matters because of this line in `talk_audio.py`:

```python
if self._echo_gate_enabled and not self._pulse_webrtc.active:
```

When `pactl` is present, the AEC route loads and the software gate is switched off entirely. On a setup like this one, installing `pulseaudio-utils` would silently trade a gate that works for a canceller that doesn't, and the self-replies would come back. Two ideas, either would have saved me here:

- an explicit switch for the AEC route (e.g. `TALK_PULSE_AEC=off`), and/or
- keeping the gate active (perhaps with relaxed thresholds) even when the AEC route is up, unless the operator turns it off.

Happy to send a PR for either if you think it fits.

**Unrelated, but it looked like the agent "freezing":** with the voice session idle for 5 minutes, GNOME blanks the screen. The HDMI TV then drops off, PipeWire falls back to the Dummy Output in the same second, and the agent keeps talking into nothing, with no error.
